Descriptive statistics table ("Table 1")

Source: R/descriptives.R
apa_descriptives.Rd

Makes an APA-style table describing a sample: for each continuous variable, its mean and standard deviation (or median and interquartile range), and for each categorical variable, the number and percentage of respondents at each level. With by, there is a column for each group and one for the whole sample, and group differences can be tested.

Usage

apa_descriptives(
  data,
  variables = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  total = TRUE,
  continuous = "mean_sd",
  categorical = NULL,
  labels = NULL,
  test = FALSE,
  categorical_test = c("auto", "chisq", "fisher"),
  missing = c("note", "row"),
  range = FALSE,
  digits = 2,
  percent_digits = 1,
  format_variable_names = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

data frame

variables

variables to describe, in order: unquoted or quoted names (e.g., c(age, income) or c("age", "income")) or tidyselect helpers (e.g., starts_with("item") or where(is.numeric)). If NULL (default), all columns. The by variable is never described.

by

grouping variable, unquoted or quoted (e.g., group or "group"). If given, each group gets a column.

total

if TRUE (default), a column for the whole sample is added when there are groups

continuous

how continuous variables are described: "mean_sd" (default) for M (SD), or "median_iqr" for Mdn (IQR). A named vector sets it for particular variables (e.g., c(income = "median_iqr")), and other variables use "mean_sd".

categorical

numeric variables to treat as categorical, selected like variables

labels

named character vector of variable labels (e.g., c(age = "Age (years)")). Variables without a label are named by their formatted names.

test

if TRUE, a column of p-values tests the differences between groups (requires by)

categorical_test

test of categorical variables when test = TRUE: "auto" (default) for Fisher's exact test when an expected count is below 5 and the chi-square test otherwise, "chisq" for the chi-square test, or "fisher" for Fisher's exact test

missing

where missing values are reported: "note" (default) in the note, or "row" in a "Missing" row below each variable that has missing values

range

if TRUE, a "Range" row with the minimum and maximum is added below each continuous variable

digits

number of decimal places of means, standard deviations, medians, interquartile ranges, and ranges

percent_digits

number of decimal places of percentages

format_variable_names

format variable names that have no label with the Variable column format

Value

apa7_tbl (tibble)

Details

Numeric variables are continuous, and factors, character vectors, and logical vectors are categorical (use categorical to treat numeric codes as categories). Each categorical variable is introduced by a heading row, with its levels indented below it, in factor level order (character vectors are sorted).

Percentages are of the nonmissing responses. By default, apa_note() lists the number of missing values of each variable that has any; with missing = "row", each such variable gets a "Missing" row with the number of missing values in each column instead. Rows whose by value is missing are left out.

With range = TRUE, each continuous variable gets a "Range" row with its minimum and maximum.

With test = TRUE, a p column tests group differences: Welch's t test (two groups) or Welch's one-way ANOVA (stats::oneway.test(), more groups) for variables described by their mean, the Kruskal-Wallis test for variables described by their median, and the chi-square test of independence (without continuity correction) for categorical variables. When an expected count of a categorical variable's table is below 5, the chi-square approximation can be poor, so by default (categorical_test = "auto") Fisher's exact test is used for that variable instead, and the note names the variables tested this way. Many journals discourage testing baseline differences in randomized trials, so tests are not shown by default.

Examples

d <- mtcars
d$am <- factor(d$am, labels = c("Automatic", "Manual"))
d$cyl <- factor(d$cyl)
apa_descriptives(d, variables = c("mpg", "hp", "cyl"), by = "am")
#> # A tibble: 6 × 4
#>   Variable        `Automatic (*n* = 19)` `Manual (*n* = 13)` `Total (*N* = 32)`
#>   <chr>           <chr>                  <chr>               <chr>             
#> 1 Mpg, *M* (*SD*) "17.15 (3.83)"         "24.39 (6.17)"      "20.09 (6.03)"    
#> 2 Hp, *M* (*SD*)  "160.26 (53.91)"       "126.85 (84.06)"    "146.69 (68.56)"  
#> 3 Cyl, *n* (%)    ""                     ""                  ""                
#> 4  4              "3 (15.8)"             "8 (61.5)"          "11 (34.4)"       
#> 5  6              "4 (21.1)"             "3 (23.1)"          "7 (21.9)"        
#> 6  8              "12 (63.2)"            "2 (15.4)"          "14 (43.8)"       

# Ranges and rows of missing values
d$hp[c(3, 8)] <- NA
apa_descriptives(d, variables = c("mpg", "hp", "cyl"), by = "am",
                 range = TRUE, missing = "row")
#> # A tibble: 9 × 4
#>   Variable        `Automatic (*n* = 19)` `Manual (*n* = 13)` `Total (*N* = 32)`
#>   <chr>           <chr>                  <chr>               <chr>             
#> 1 Mpg, *M* (*SD*) "17.15 (3.83)"         "24.39 (6.17)"      "20.09 (6.03)"    
#> 2  Range          "10.40–24.40"          "15.00–33.90"       "10.40–33.90"     
#> 3 Hp, *M* (*SD*)  "165.72 (49.77)"       "129.67 (87.16)"    "151.30 (68.24)"  
#> 4  Range          "95.00–245.00"         "52.00–335.00"      "52.00–335.00"    
#> 5  Missing        "1"                    "1"                 "2"               
#> 6 Cyl, *n* (%)    ""                     ""                  ""                
#> 7  4              "3 (15.8)"             "8 (61.5)"          "11 (34.4)"       
#> 8  6              "4 (21.1)"             "3 (23.1)"          "7 (21.9)"        
#> 9  8              "12 (63.2)"            "2 (15.4)"          "14 (43.8)"       

# Unquoted names and tidyselect helpers work too
apa_descriptives(d, variables = c(mpg, starts_with("c")), by = am)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 4
#>   Variable         `Automatic (*n* = 19)` `Manual (*n* = 13)` `Total (*N* = 32)`
#>   <chr>            <chr>                  <chr>               <chr>             
#> 1 Mpg, *M* (*SD*)  "17.15 (3.83)"         "24.39 (6.17)"      "20.09 (6.03)"    
#> 2 Cyl, *n* (%)     ""                     ""                  ""                
#> 3  4               "3 (15.8)"             "8 (61.5)"          "11 (34.4)"       
#> 4  6               "4 (21.1)"             "3 (23.1)"          "7 (21.9)"        
#> 5  8               "12 (63.2)"            "2 (15.4)"          "14 (43.8)"       
#> 6 Carb, *M* (*SD*) "2.74 (1.15)"          "2.92 (2.18)"       "2.81 (1.62)"     

# Medians for skewed variables, and tests of group differences
apa_descriptives(
  d,
  variables = c(mpg, hp, cyl),
  by = am,
  continuous = c(hp = "median_iqr"),
  test = TRUE
)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>   Variable   `Automatic (*n* = 19)` `Manual (*n* = 13)` `Total (*N* = 32)` `*p*`
#>   <chr>      <chr>                  <chr>               <chr>              <chr>
#> 1 Mpg, *M* … "17.15 (3.83)"         "24.39 (6.17)"      "20.09 (6.03)"     ".00…
#> 2 Hp, *Mdn*… "175.00 (75.75)"       "109.50 (62.50)"    "136.50 (74.00)"   ".04…
#> 3 Cyl, *n* … ""                     ""                  ""                 ".00…
#> 4  4         "3 (15.8)"             "8 (61.5)"          "11 (34.4)"        ""   
#> 5  6         "4 (21.1)"             "3 (23.1)"          "7 (21.9)"         ""   
#> 6  8         "12 (63.2)"            "2 (15.4)"          "14 (43.8)"        ""
